full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J.: This criminal appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order of acquittal dated 27.04.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Appeal No.2767 of 1998 and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 04.10.1998 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.2, Bogra in Sessions Case No.22 of 1994 convicting the present respondent under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to suffer' rigorous imprisonment for life with a fine of Tk.5000/- in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more. 

 2. Facts leading to the disposal of the appeal are that one Bhanu Chandra Das as informant lodged an ejahar with Bogra Police Station on 08.04.1992 at 08.25 hours stating interalia that on 07.04.1992 corresponding to 24 Chaitra, 1398 at about 8.00 p.m. the accused named in the FIR alongwith other 20/22 persons attacked the inhabitants of Thanthania village and beat them indiscriminately, damaged some houses and shops; Being afraid, local people ran away helter and shelter; At that time victim Palash Chandra, son of the informant was standing in front of the shop of his brother; The victim Palash being terrified ran away towards the east when the accused persons chased him and assaulted him severely at Battala of the village; Accused Nashu dealt Ramdao blow on the left abdomen of the victim Palash causing grievous injury as a result his intestine came out; On hearing hue and cry, the witnesses came forward and the accused-persons fled away; Being asked by the informant the victim stated that accused Nashu injured him with ramdao blow; The victim was brought to the Mohammad Ali Hospital, Bogra, wherein he succumbed to his injury at about 1.00 a.m. following the night of 07.04.1992; Many people including Gouranga, Ranjit, Tunu, Sukamal, Bidhan saw the occurrence. On the basis of the ejahar, Bogra Police Station Case No.02 dated 08.04.1992 under sections 148/302/34 of the Penal Code was registered. The post-mortem of the victim was conducted by the civil surgeon of Bogra who found following injury: 

 6. The learned Sessions Judge, Bogra, took cognizance of the offence against the accused persons and transferred the case in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.2, Bogra, for trial. 

 8. The prosecution examined as many as 17 (seventeen) witnesses. The defence examined none. But from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses it appears that the defence case is of total denial who, claimed that they are falsely implicated in the case out of previous enmity. 

 9. After examining prosecution witnesses, the accused present on the dock namely Nashu and Mosha alias Shahjahan were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the prosecution case briefly narrated to them but again they pleaded their innocence. These two accused persons recorded statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 13. Mr. S. M. Munir, learned Additional Attorney General appearing on behalf of the State submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts and circumstances of the case in its true perspective which results serious miscarriage of justice. He also submits that despite confessional statement recorded by the respondent under section 164 the Code of Criminal Procedure the High Court Division was not justified in setting aside the conviction and sentence. 

 17. The informant PW.1 in his deposition reiterated the statement made in the FIR. In his cross-examination he stated that after primary treatment in the hospital the victim opened his eyes and spoke but at that time he was not there, he went to bring medicine. He denied the suggestion that he has good relationship with Mahbubur Rahman who influenced him to file false case against Ripon and others due to enmity. 

 28. PW.12 Shukamal Das deposed that on hearing hue and cry he went to the place of occurrence and saw the injured victim. He also deposed that he and Bhanu Chandra Das brought the victim to the hospital and admitted in emergency wherein the duty doctor declared him death. He further deposed that the victim did not say any name. In his cross-examination he stated that the accused Swapan, Ripon and Sagar were witnesses in the case filed by Direndra Nath Das against him and he was convicted in that case. He stated that he did not see the occurrence. 

 37. In many of the cases our Apex Court held that wherein the accused was kept in police custody for 3(three) days preceding his confession cannot made the confessional statement voluntary and true and therefore the conviction is unwarranted. We have also perused the deposition of the PW. 1, father of the victim, who deposed that his deceased son told him that Nashu dealt him with ramdao and other accused assaulted him but another son of the PW.1 who is full brother of the victim deposed as PW.2 before the Court refuting the testimony of his father. The dying declaration of the victim before the PW.8 Dr. Md. Mamunur Rashid in the hospital, exhibit-3, is as follows: 

 38. From the above quoted statement it is apparent that the victim stated that the companions of Nashu inflicted the ramdao injury and Nashu was there alongwith them. In the case of Tawaib Khan and another vs. The State reported in 22 DLR(SC)16, their lordships observed that "a dying declaration can be relied on with specific narration for assessing the guilt of the accused persons." We have also noticed discrepancy in the deposition of PW.8 Dr. Md. Mamunur Rashid who conducted the post-mortem examination. Apart from that we find from the evidence that all the prosecution witnesses admittedly are interrelated but their deposition favour the accused persons. 

 39. In convicting a person under section 302 the guilt against him must be proved beyond reasonable doubt but on perusal of the evidence on record we do not find that the prosecution has been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
